NOTES ON GAMES AND ATHLETICS. FOOTBALL. Those who have followed the play of- Oldham this season fully expected that Warrington would have to put in all they knew in order to win, but at the same time it was fully expected, in Warrington, at all events, that the wirepullers would come out uppermost. Great was the surprise and disappointment therefore, when it was seen towards the end of the game that the spindle- tonians had got a gal in advance and that there was very little prospect of the local players pulling even. As a rule, the Warrington team out-stay their opponents, and show up best towards the end of the game, but on Saturday the Oldham forwards showed unexpected stay- ing qualities, and when once they had got the lead they managed to keep it till the end of the game. Warrington were unfortunate in not being able to put their full team in the field, both Boscow and Lawless be- ing away. Webster made a good substitute for the ab- sent three-quarter, but Boscow's cool head and unfailing judgment were badly missed at full back. Sampson is a smart "A" team back, but it was rather unfortunate that he had to be called upon for a ticklish first team match like that against Oldham. It is almost certain that had Boscow been in his usual place, the visitors I would never have had a chance of scoring the winning point, and perhaps might not have equalised. To-day the Warringtonians have another tough en- ' counter before them against St. Helens Recs. There has always been a keen but friendly rivalry between these two teams, an'd their matches are usually fraught with excitement and good play. There is sure to be another "big gate." --- In Yorkshire, football was, on Saturday, carried on ander difficulties, heavy rain sadly interfering with play as a rule. Bradford demonstrated their superiority over Wakefield Trinity, as was fully exnected. Halifax were too good for Huddersfield, but they were unable to con- vert any of their three tries into goals. Some of the games were very closely contested. Leeds, for instance, had only a try the best of it with Manningham, Batley being similarly successful over Hull, and Dewsbury over Heckmondwike. In fact the scoring was low all round. As Derby County were not figurine,' in the League competition on Saturday, the match at Birmingham be- tween Aston Villa and the Bolton Wanderers resolved itself into a struggle for the first place. Both clubs were credited with eight points, and it was generally antici- pated that the Wanderers would be sent home beaten. But to everybody's astonishment they overplayed the home team and deservedly won by two goals to one. The latter point was given to the Villa, owing to a blun- der by one of the Bolton backs. The victors played really admirable football,and they must now be regarded as one of the most formidable of the fourteen clubs in the League. It was quite in the fitness of things that the North And should escape defeat at Anfield Road. Somehow, Everton invariably find their match in the Preston team, and were twice vanquished by them in League fixtures last season. The Liverpool club had now to do without Geary, and were soon deprived of the services of Camp- bell, full back, owing to a mishap. On the other hand, the North End had the valued assistance of N. J. Ross once more, and they managed to make a draw of it, a goal being scored by each side. The Blackburn Rovers added a win to their credit, scoring two goals to none at Ewood Park against Wolverhampton Wanderers. Rose's goal-keeping for the " Wolves ' was splendid. Mason, who, it was stated, had retired fram the game, again turned out for the visitors. Darwen gained another point by drawing with Accrington, one goal being ob- tained by each side. A decided reverse awaited Burnley at Stoke, the Lancashire club being defeated by three goals to none. Worse still was the experience of the West Bromwich Albion, who were disposed of by Notts County by four to none. All the three Birmingham dis- trict clubs—the Villa, the Albion, and Wolverhampton— lost their League fixtures. Sam Thompson, the well known centre forward, is about to make another change. He was first connected with Preston North End, thence removed to Wolver- hampton, next to Everton, and now he is going to Accrington, so that he will have played with four League clubs.
